Due to health recommendations from the Center for Disease Control and State of California
Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), and the declared state of emergency
wherein social distancing measures have been imposed or recommended, the CITY OF
AVALON’S CITY COUNCIL and PLANNING COMMISSION MEETINGS SHALL GENERALLY
BE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC REMOTELY. The general public may attend the meeting in
the Council Chambers however must adhere to social distancing requirements. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes while practicing social
distancing.

Chambers reach maximum occupancy, the general public may participate in Oral

admitted into the Council Chambers who is ill or exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19. Additionally,
the general public may participate in Oral Communication and address the City Council on an
agenda items by providing comments via Zoom or by sending comments to
askcityofavalon.com.

3.  Board of Directors Appointment for the Gateway Cities Council of Governments
  The Gateway Cities Council of Governments is comprised of 32 cities in the southeast
  Los Angeles County region. The Board of Directors has a City Council representative
  from each of the represented cities as well as the Mayor of Long Beach and three
  members of the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors and a representative from the
  Port of Long Beach.
  Recommended Action
  Appoint Councilmember Lisa Lavelle to represent the City of Avalon on the Board of
  Directors for the Gateway Cities Council of Governments.

4.  League of California Cities Annual Voting Delegate
  The Annual League of California Cities Conference will be held in Long Beach, California
  from September 7 to 9, 2022. An important part of the conference is the Annual Business
  Meeting. At this business meeting, the League membership considers and takes action
  on resolutions that establish League Policy. In order to vote at the Business Meeting, City
  Council must designate a voting delegate and an alternate voting delegate.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution appointing Mayor Marshall as the voting delegate and Mayor ProTem
  Michael Ponce as an alternate voting for the Annual League of California Cities
  Conference in September 2022.

5.  Authorize Voting Delegate for Los Angeles Division League of California Cities Division
  Installation
  The Los Angeles Division Annual Installation Ceremony and Dinner will take place on
  August 4, 2022 in Diamond Bar, CA. Councilmember Ponce plans to attend the meeting
  and requested permission to represent the City of Avalon and participate in the meeting
  as a voting delegate.
  Recommended Action
  Designate Councilmember Michael Ponce as the City’s representative and authorize him
  to vote during the Los Angeles Division League of California Cities Installation meeting
  on August 4, 2022.

6.  Denial of Appeal #22-01 Regarding Planning Commission Action of PC #2783 Approving
  a Setback Variance at 261 F. Whittley
  During the July 19, 2022 meeting, the City Council denied an appeal regarding Planning
  Commission approval of a setback variance oat 261 F. Whittley.

  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution formally denying Appeal #22-01 and setting forth findings made.

GENERAL BUSINESS

7.  First Reading of an Ordinance Amending Chapter 9-7.10A02 of Title 9, Planning and
  Zoning, of the Avalon Municipal Code Relating to Temporary Use Permits
  The City adopted the Temporary Use Ordinance during its March 7, 2017 regular City
  Council meeting. The ordinance was established to address instances when the City
  received a land use request that was not necessarily permitted within a specific zone, but
  which the City may be inclined to allow.
  Recommended Action
  Introduce and waive all readings of an ordinance of the City of Avalon amending Chapter
  9-7.10A02 of Title 9, Planning and Zoning, of the Avalon Municipal Code Relating to
  Temporary Use Permits.

8.  Discuss Chapter 6, Section 6.13 of the Avalon Municipal Code Regarding Water
  Conservation and Phase One Enforcement of Fresh Water Conservation
  In 2001 the City ofAvalon adopted an urgency ordinance (Ordinance #997-O1U, effective
  January 17, 2001) establishing legislation regarding mandatory conservation measures
  that will be implemented when Southern California Edison (SCE) begins “Phase One”
  water conservation and a penalty for non-compliance.
  Recommended Action
  Discuss Chapter 6, Section 6.13 of the Avalon Municipal Code regarding water
  conservation and enforcement of Phase One water conservation. Provide direction to
  Staff.

SUBJECT:  Board of Directors Appointment for the Gateway Cities Council of
  Governments

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Appoint Councilmember Lisa Lavelle to represent the City of
Avalon on the Board of Directors for the Gateway Cities Council of Governments.

REPORT SUMMARY: The Gateway Cities Council of Governments is comprised of 32 cities in
the southeast Los Angeles County region. The Board of Directors has a City Council
representative from each of the represented cities as well as the Mayor of Long Beach and three
members of the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors and a representative from the Port of
Long Beach.

The Gateway Cities Council of Governments is involved in a number of regional initiatives and
planning efforts, but the mission of the organization is primarily focused on transportation, air
quality, housing and economic development matters. Former Mayor Pro Tem Cinde MacGugan
Cassidy served as the City of Avalons representative since 2014. Councilmember Lisa Lavelle
has expressed an interest in serving as the Board of Director’s Representative.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Professional development.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Funds have been allocated in the budget to maintain membership and for
a member of City Council to affend monthly meetings of the Gateway Cities Council of
Governments in Paramount, CA. (Account #10110-5510)

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City of Avalon will
not have a representative on the Board of Directors for Gateway Cities Council of Governments.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Direct the City Clerk to contact the Gateway Cities Council of
Governments and notify them of the City’s representative for the Board of Directors.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: Pursuant to the Brown Act.

REPORT SUMMARY: On April 20! 2022, the Planning Commission took action on a request for
approval of a Site Plan and a Setback Variance at 261 E. Whittley for the ongoing remodel of a
duplex in the Medium Density Residential zone.

On May 3, 2022 Charles Canby, and other surrounding property owners, filed a timely appeal
(Appeal #22-01) of the Planning commission’s decision, requesting that the City council hear
the Project de novo at a public hearing.

meeting. City Council requested more information from City Staff and the matter was continued
to June 21, 2022. At the June 21, 2022 meeting no new information or testimony was provided
and the item was continued to the July 19, 2022 regular meeting of the City Council.

During the July 19, 2022 meeting, the City Council denied the appeal! and established the
condition that the property owner at 261 E. Whittley was not permitted to increase the square
footage of the site plan currently on file with the Planning Department.

City Staff recommend the City Council’s denial of the appeal and additional conditions be
formally memorialized by resolution.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Introduce and waive all readings of an ordinance of the City of
Avalon amending Chapter 9-7.10A02 of Title 9, Planning and Zoning, of the Avalon Municipal
Code Relating to Temporary Use Permits.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City adopted the Temporary Use Ordinance during its March 7,
2017 regular City Council meeting. The ordinance was established to address instances when
the City received a land use request that was not necessarily permitted within a specific zone,
but which the City may be inclined to allow. At the time the City did not have a formal process
for reviewing and issuing temporary use permits.

The adopted ordinance allowed the City Manager to grant temporary use permits for any use
that is:
  1. For a specified and limited duration of time.
  2. Consistent with the general purposes of the General Plan.
  3. Consistent with the health, safety and welfare of the surrounding community.
  4. Not otherwise permitted within the specific zone.

Additionally, the ordinance requires the City Manager make the following findings in order to
approve a temporary use permit:
  -  The operation and maintenance of the use will be conducted so as to minimize the
  impact on existing uses on adjoining properties and in the surrounding areas.
  -  The temporary use will have adequate parking, ingress and egress, traffic circulation
  and access, and provisions for pedestrian safety.
  -  All structures and equipment are erected and maintained in compliance with the
  Municipal Code.
  -  The subject site will be restored to its original or better condition upon termination of the
  temporary use.
  -  The temporary use is not detrimental to the public health, safety and welfare and
  specific identifiable benefits to the City of Avalon and its residents.

As the City Manager approves the permits, he also has the authority to impose additional
conditions.
 When the original ordinance was introduced, the City Council requested the ordinance include
a provision that would sunset the process after two years if not extended by the City Council.

City Staff recommend extending this ordinance and permitting process without a provision that
will sunset it in the future.

REPORT SUMMARY: This item appears on the agenda at the request of a member of the City
Council.

In 2001 the City of Avalon adopted an urgency ordinance (Ordinance #997-O1U, effective
January 17, 2001) establishing legislation regarding mandatory conservation measures that will
be implemented when Southern California Edison (SCE) begins “Phase One” water
conservation.

Per the Ordinance:

Until such time that Southern California Edison or other provider of freshwater to consumers
within the City of Avalon, has lifted Phase One of the Santa Catalina Island Fresh Water
Rationing Plan (the ‘Plan’) as set forth in Rule 14.1 of the tariff issued by the California Public
Utilities Commission, it shall be unlawful for any person to cause or to permit to be caused, any
use of freshwater sup plied by such provided, as follows:

  (a) The washing of streets, driveways, parking lots, patios, piers, sidewalks, tennis courts,
  walkways, and other hard-surfaced areas by hosing or by use of fresh water directly from
  faucets or other outlets, except where done by means of a bucket or container not
  exceeding a three gallon capacity;
  (b) The washing of motor vehicles, trailers, boats, golf carts, or airplanes by hosing or by use
  of fresh water directly from faucets or other outlets, except where done by means of a
  bucket or container not exceeding a three gallon capacity;
  (c) The use of fresh water from fire hydrants for any purpose other than fire suppression;
  (d) The use of fresh water for soil compaction;
  (e) Watering of outdoor landscaping and vegetation by hoses or sprinkling systems except
  between the hours of 7:00 a. m. to 9:00 a. m. and 5:00p.m. to 7:00 p.m. during the period
  that Pacific Daylight Time is in effect, and from 6:00 am. to 8:00 am. and 4:00 p.m. to
   6:00 p.m. during the period that Pacific Standard Time is in effect. Watering by use of a
  bucket or container not exceeding a three gallon capacity is permitted at any time.
  (f) The service of drinking water to a customer at any restaurant or bar or other place which
  serves food and/or beverages except upon request by such person. Businesses subject
  to this subsection shall post notice thereof in a conspicuous place, bearing language
  similar to the following: “In order to conserve Avalon’s limited fresh water supply, water
  is served upon request only.”

The City of Avalon shall be exempt from the provisions of § 6-6.13, but the City Manager shall
implement all reasonable measures to conserve freshwater use by the City.

A first violation of this section shall be punishable as an infraction, subject to a $50 fine. A second
violation committed within 12 months of the first violation, and any subsequent violations
thereafter, shall be punishable as a misdemeanor

The California Public Utility Commission has authorized SCE to begin Phase One water
conservation as outlined in Rule 14.1 of the tariff effective July 10, 2022. SCE has indicated they
